The smaller relative mobility of calcium and magnesium in the environment of the ephemeral springs than in the environment of perennial springs implies selective removal of sodium where the activity of the hydrogen ion is high. The median pH of the ephemeral- spring water (table 2) is lower than that of the perennial springs. As hydrogen-ion activity lessens and pH rises, the rate of removal of sodium from mineral molecules seems to decrease. In turn, the percentage of the alkaline earths in water increases, and their apparent relative mobility likewise rises. That sodium is the most mobile of the elements in waters from granodiorite is unexpected.
